$comment: EXAMPLE fleet record (ADR-004). Copy to instances.json (gitignored) and fill in your own
AWS account, region, domain and Terraform state bucket. The real instances.json is never
committed; instance.mjs and terraform/instances/dev/locals.tf fall back to this example when
it is absent (so CI — which uses -backend=false + a mocked provider — runs on placeholders).
domain.aliases.<service> lists extra hostnames served by the same API (ADR-016 §2); the short <service>.responsive.city names live here while the *-mcp names stay the primary domain.
cdcDomainName / cdcService: the OpenContext portal Lambda for data.cdc.gov (ADR-016 §5), serving the CDC PLACES source guide.
hudDomainName / hudService: the HUD User server (M11, ADR-018); its primary hostname is already the short hud-user.responsive.city name.
beaDomainName / beaService: the BEA Regional server (M14, ADR-019), at the short bea.responsive.city name.

limits.<service>: public-use protection (#319, ADR-020 §2, §6, §7) — stage throttling, Lambda reserved concurrency and the in-app FEDERAL_MCPS_LIMITS budget. Optional; every field shown here is also each terraform module's own default (ADR-020's question-5 table), so this block can be omitted entirely — it is spelled out so a self-hoster sees the shape and can override a field by editing their own instances.json.

instances.name: dev
instances.description: federal-mcps dev in the Responsive City account
